problem: Token merging accelerates Transformers by reducing sequence length, but induces covariate shift and performance collapse under aggressive compression due to energy drift and biased attention distributions.
approach: Reframe token merging as statistical reconstruction and introduce asymptotic radial-angular decomposition to decouple magnitude and distributional distortions, yielding a single scaling factor correction √r.
contribution: Closed-form optimal corrections calibrate both energy balance and distributional fidelity, demonstrating superior accuracy and robustness across compression levels on vision Transformers.

problem: Reference-guided video editing requires faithful application of text instructions while preserving motion and content, but existing methods suffer from modality gaps (decoupled encoders) or loss of spatial details (unified encoders).
approach: MiVE repurposes vision-language models as multiscale feature extractors, hierarchically extracting features from early layers (spatial details) and deeper layers (semantic understanding) and integrating them into a unified diffusion transformer.
contribution: MiVE achieves state-of-the-art performance in reference-guided video editing, ranking highest in human preference over both academic methods and commercial systems.

problem: Small language models lag behind larger counterparts in reasoning; existing fixes either invoke expensive LLMs at reasoning divergence or rely on limited distillation.
approach: Identify local sufficiency where LLM's preferred token resides in SLM's top-K predictions; propose Select to Think (S2T) to reframe LLM as selector among SLM proposals and distill selection logic into SLM via discrete ranking supervision.
contribution: S2T-Local improves 1.5B SLM's Math Avg. by 24.1% relative gain over greedy decoding, matching 8-path self-consistency with single-trajectory efficiency.

problem: Understanding educational social dynamics faces a fundamental dilemma: observational studies lack causal power while controlled experiments face ethical constraints.
approach: EduMirror provides a multi-agent simulator with value-driven agents grounded in psychological needs and a dual-track measurement protocol for observable behaviors and latent psychological states.
contribution: EduMirror generates educational social dynamics that are realistic, theory-consistent, and measurable, enabling in silico hypothesis testing and counterfactual intervention analysis.

problem: Black-box optimization of Lipschitz functions under noise lacks explicit optimality certificates and measurable progress guarantees.
approach: Certificate-Guided Pruning (CGP) maintains an active set of potentially optimal points via confidence-adjusted Lipschitz envelopes, with theoretical convergence under margin conditions.
contribution: CGP achieves sample complexity Õ(ε^-(2+α)) and demonstrates strong empirical performance across 12 benchmarks with principled stopping criteria.

problem: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM inference but judge-based verification relies on human annotations or verifiable ground truths, limiting generalizability across diverse NLP tasks.
approach: SelfJudge trains judge verifiers via self-supervision of the target model by assessing semantic preservation through token-substituted response analysis.
contribution: SelfJudge achieves superior inference-accuracy trade-offs over judge baselines and generalizes broadly across diverse NLP tasks without ground truth annotations.

problem: Building omni-modal assistants via end-to-end multimodal alignment incurs substantial data and compute costs while limiting extensibility.
approach: LLM Orchestration integrates off-the-shelf modality experts without gradient-based training via an LLM controller for expert selection, text-centric cross-modal memory for compression, and unified interaction layer for streaming support.
contribution: LLM Orchestration achieves strong performance on multimodal benchmarks with low overhead and modular upgradeability, providing practical alternative to costly joint training.

problem: Subjective LLM evaluation faces a reproducibility crisis where even the same evaluator contradicts itself on re-judging samples due to dimension drift in free-form protocols.
approach: Reformulate subjective evaluation as information-theoretic optimization using Expected Information Gain (EIG) framework to construct stable yet adaptive rubrics that eliminate dimension drift.
contribution: EIG-based approach substantially improves evaluation consistency and alignment with human judgments on six benchmarks including CharacterEval and MT-Bench, outperforming CoT and fixed-questionnaire baselines.

problem: Audio self-supervised learning models rely on finetuning for evaluation because simple probing fails to unlock their full potential and alters model rankings on AudioSet.
approach: Introduce Convex Gated Probing (CGP), a prototype-based method using gating to efficiently utilize frozen layers and expose latent task-relevant information.
contribution: Better Audio Transformer (BAT) refined via CGP establishes new state-of-the-art on audio benchmarks through improved preprocessing, architecture, and pretraining recipe.

problem: In multi-model self-consuming training regimes where models learn from each other's outputs, human curation of one model may dampen or invert alignment effects rather than consistently enhance them.
approach: Formalize multi-model self-consuming framework, characterize convergence dynamics, and analyze self-influence (local curation impact) versus cross-influence (propagation to other models).
contribution: Cross-model interactions can degrade long-term alignment despite local curation benefits, revealing fundamental limits of human curation in interconnected systems.

problem: Existing disease prediction models depend on event-level healthcare representations and lack explicit modeling of social determinants of health (SDoH), limiting personalized disease modeling.
approach: DiffDT integrates multi-organ sensor data with diffusion models and geometric diffusion for brain networks, conditioned on ICD-coded SDoH proxies for disease trajectory simulation.
contribution: DiffDT achieves significant improvements over autoregressive baselines on UK Biobank with multi-organ imaging and medical history data for in silico disease reasoning.

problem: LoRA convergence analysis is poorly understood due to lack of Lipschitz smoothness, with existing results only addressing asymptotic behavior or assuming strong boundedness.
approach: Provide non-asymptotic convergence analysis by reformulating LoRA in terms of outer product of stacked adapter matrices and applying modified descent lemma for reparametrized function.
contribution: LoRA gradient descent converges to stationary point at rate O(1/log T) without Lipschitz smoothness assumptions, reflecting actual practice.

problem: Vision-language models fail to generate personalized responses based on user-specific visual-textual context due to inability to associate visual inputs with accumulated experience.
approach: CoViP treats personalized image captioning as core task and improves through reinforcement-learning-based post-training and caption-augmented generation with diagnostic evaluations ruling out textual shortcuts.
contribution: CoViP improves personalized image captioning and yields holistic gains across downstream personalization tasks, with existing VLMs showing substantial limitations on visual context leveraging.

problem: Transformers for evidence-grounded binary adjudication are sensitive to evidence order, producing unreliable answers; token-level training minimizes expected description length but remains position-sensitive at fixed orderings.
approach: Formalize expectation-realization gap via Quantified Martingale Violation (QMV) bound and Expectation-level Decompression Law (EDFL), yielding information-theoretic gates (B2T, RoH, ISR) for answer/abstain decisions.
contribution: On 3,059 grounded items, ISR=1 gate achieves 0.0-0.7% hallucination with 20.6-27.9% abstention (95% CIs) without universal calibration claims.

problem: Long video understanding requires balancing cloud-based reasoning quality against prohibitive bandwidth costs and latency, with edge solutions sacrificing accuracy.
approach: SCOPE decomposes complex queries into a structured DAG observation plan via cloud LMM, guiding edge retrieval by logical necessity rather than statistical similarity.
contribution: SCOPE matches cloud-level accuracy with significantly lower transmission costs and outperforms baselines on Video-MME and LongVideoBench complex reasoning tasks.

problem: Chain-of-Thought reasoning in autoregressive LLMs remains brittle under distribution shift and long-horizon generation, with small deviations compounding into inference drift.
approach: Thinking in Flow (TiF) augments Transformers with persistent continuous-time thought state governed by dissipative ODE dynamics, with demand-supply gates determining when and how to intervene.
contribution: TiF improves robustness to distractions and semantic perturbations while maintaining or improving accuracy on mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Single predictors deployed across multiple subpopulations require fairness approaches that account for different potential predictability levels across groups.
approach: Interpret group fairness as bargaining problem; propose relative improvement (ratio of actual to potential risk reduction), recovering Kalai-Smorodinsky solution with scale invariance and individual monotonicity.
contribution: Relative improvement provides axiomatic fairness justification and establishes finite-sample convergence guarantees under mild conditions.

problem: Autoregressive LLMs fail in complex reasoning because early-stage errors remain uncorrectable due to irreversibility in Transformer architecture.
approach: HEdit detects internal inconsistency at trigger points, backtracks to critical anchors, and uses lightweight trainable editor to refine Key-Value caches during generation.
contribution: HEdit improves mathematical reasoning by 2.2-10.8% with <0.5% added parameters, providing dynamic pluggable solution for low-resource environments.

problem: Training data reconstruction from KKT conditions shows empirical success but lacks clarity on when equations have unique solutions and how to reliably recover them.
approach: Provide sufficient conditions for KKT identifiability in two-layer networks with polynomial activations; introduce sample splitting for curvature-aware refinement escaping poor stationary points.
contribution: Sample splitting consistently improves reconstruction performance across multiple reconstruction methods on real datasets.

problem: Retrieval-Augmented Generation suffers from prohibitive computational costs when incorporating large document volumes; existing compression heuristics compromise task performance.
approach: CORE-RAG uses performance-driven learning with task performance as feedback signal, with knowledge distillation initialization for robust policy learning.
contribution: At 3% compression ratio, CORE improves average EM score by 3.3 points compared to using full documents without performance degradation.

problem: Pre-Layer Normalization is standard but incurs statistical-computation overhead and suffers from curse of depth where hidden-state magnitudes grow with layer count, destabilizing training.
approach: Bounded Hyperbolic Tanh (BHyT) combines tanh nonlinearity with data-driven input bounding to keep activations in non-saturating range, computing exact statistics once per block with lightweight variance approximation.
contribution: BHyT achieves 1.6% faster training and 1.77% higher token throughput versus RMSNorm while maintaining strong pretraining and post-SFT performance.

problem: Estimating kernel means efficiently for query points requires bounds that improve in regimes with small error and intermediate diameter.
approach: Prove new bound Õ(d + ε∆²+1/ε³) for Gaussian kernel estimation via fast spherical embedding theorem that preserves local distances while limiting embedded diameter.
contribution: New bound improves over previous Õ(d+1/ε⁴) and Õ(d+∆²/ε²) in small-error and intermediate-diameter regimes.

problem: Hypergraph Neural Networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks but lack adversarial training mechanisms; existing attacks are white-box and customized for specific perturbation types.
approach: Propose MeLA, a generic meta-objective-based gray-box attack framework leveraging hypergraph Laplacian for structural and feature perturbations; develop adversarial training mechanism with convergence guarantees.
contribution: Adversarial training enhances HGNN defense and MeLA attacks are effective in poisoning and evasion settings across various models and datasets.

problem: Multi-modal brain network analysis treats phenotypes only as auxiliary features and assumes connectome should be learned uniformly across phenotypes, ignoring context-dependent interpretations.
approach: PhenoBrain injects phenotype information at mechanism level via phenotype-conditioned long-range routing kernel and phenotypic-guided attention regulation.
contribution: PhenoBrain achieves state-of-the-art performance on multi-modal brain network analysis datasets with phenotype-conditioned architecture.

problem: Supervised graph outlier detection suffers from severe class imbalance; diffusion-based augmentation improves sample quality but incurs prohibitive multi-step computational costs.
approach: GOCM proposes single-step graph outlier synthesis via consistency model with Origin Consistency mechanism using Interval-based Origin Inference; MiVGAE handles heterogeneous graphs.
contribution: GOCM achieves superior detection performance with significantly improved generation efficiency compared to multi-step diffusion methods.

problem: Thinking with Images (TWI) for multimodal reasoning assumes interleaved chain-of-thought is faultless, but imperfect visual cue mining and reasoning cause error accumulation.
approach: RTWI estimates reliability of visual cues and textual reasoning in unified text-centric manner, employing robust filtering and voting modules to prevent noisy thinking.
contribution: RTWI demonstrates effectiveness against noisy thinking on seven benchmarks, preventing error accumulation from contaminating final answers.

problem: Inference-time steering relies on activation addition which alters hidden-state magnitudes, raising concerns about representation collapse and degraded open-ended generation.
approach: Spherical Steering rotates activations along geodesic toward target direction, preserving signal integrity; incorporates confidence gate dynamically modulating steering strength based on input uncertainty.
contribution: Spherical Steering outperforms addition-based baselines by +10% on TruthfulQA, COPA, and Storycloze while maintaining general generation quality.

problem: Multi-modal object re-identification uses MLLMs to generate text annotations as supervision but treats strong and weak correspondence image-text pairs equally, limiting discriminative learning.
approach: CCL framework explicitly models correspondence degree via Correspondence-Guided Semantic Refinement and Cognitive-Driven Dynamic Optimization modules for progressive learning.
contribution: CCL enhances feature-level alignment and optimization adaptivity, yielding robust and discriminative multi-modal representations.

problem: Autonomous GUI agents struggle with multi-step tasks due to constrained context windows and static policies failing to adapt to dynamic environments.
approach: SE-GA integrates hierarchical memory with iterative self-improvement; Test-Time Memory Extension (TTME) retrieves episodic/semantic/experiential memories; Memory-Augmented Self-Evolution (MASE) trains via collected data.
contribution: SE-GA achieves 89.0% on ScreenSpot and 75.8% on AndroidControl-High, with superior generalization on AndroidWorld benchmark.

problem: Message-passing neural networks suffer from information bottleneck and oversquashing when capturing long-range dependencies; spectral filtering enables global mixing but requires restrictive stability assumptions.
approach: S³GNN mitigates oversquashing by lightweightly reintroducing omitted components with lower complexity while maintaining effective stability constraints on feature transformations.
contribution: S³GNN achieves up to order-of-magnitude error reduction with up to 50% fewer parameters across diverse domains including long-range benchmarks and mesh-based dynamics.

problem: Fairness constraints in neural networks traditionally operate at prediction time but lack provable guarantees for streaming predictions with small batch sizes.
approach: Introduce fairness layer as differentiable optimization layer appended to output layer that guarantees output parity; develop online primal-dual inference algorithm for streaming predictions.
contribution: Fairness layer provides provable aggregate fairness guarantees and differentiability properties during backpropagation, validated through numerical experiments.

problem: Extreme model compression aims to realize spectral energy gain where low-rank binary approximations outperform tiny-rank floating-point, but latent geometry misalignment prevents realization.
approach: LittleBit-2 employs Internal Latent Rotation and Joint Iterative Quantization (Joint-ITQ) to align coherent latent distributions with binary hypercube as geometric preconditioner.
contribution: LittleBit-2 establishes new state-of-the-art in sub-1-bit regime (1~0.1 bpp) on Llama-2 and Llama-3, matching fidelity of leading 1-bit baselines.

problem: Federated recommender systems represent each user with single embedding, assuming fixed preferences; limited client data renders point estimates brittle.
approach: Model user preferences as distributions rather than points using diffusion-based generative framework, aggregating predictions across diverse embeddings to preserve uncertainty and diversity.
contribution: Distributional formulation yields more stable ranking behavior and improved robustness under ambiguous feedback on federated recommendation benchmarks.

problem: Prompt tuning of CLIP-like models is sensitive to label noise as mislabeled samples generate disproportionately large gradients that overwhelm pre-trained priors.
approach: Double-Softmax Prompt Tuning (DSPT) applies sequential probabilistic normalization inducing self-adaptive saturation zone that suppresses gradients from high-error noisy samples.
contribution: DSPT achieves state-of-the-art robustness across noisy benchmarks without hyperparameters, transforming gradient vanishing into principled noise-filtering shield.

problem: Network pruning improves efficiency but pruned models often fail in generative language tasks despite performing well in non-generative tasks; this discrepancy is poorly understood.
approach: Analyze pruning from representation-hierarchy perspective, decomposing computation into embedding/logit/probability spaces and tracking how pruning perturbations amplify through nonlinearities.
contribution: Shows stability of embedding and logit spaces enables pruning for retrieval/classification but probability-space amplification degrades generation; provides practical pruning guidance.

problem: Steering LLM reasoning trajectories toward truth is underexplored; naive representation editing through fixed steering vectors risks collateral damage to correct reasoning paths.
approach: DynaSteer employs pattern clustering to disentangle reasoning manifolds, uses Fisher-LDA to project purified truth, and dynamically monitors lookahead entropy for selective steering.
contribution: DynaSteer improves reasoning on MATH benchmarks and demonstrates generalization to out-of-domain coding tasks via dynamic representation editing.

problem: Model merging assumes improvements at fine-tuning stage propagate downstream, but long fine-tuning of experts for individual performance degrades merging due to memorization.
approach: Show late fine-tuning memorizes difficult examples creating negative parameter interference; propose task-dependent aggressive early stopping to improve model merging.
contribution: Early stopping strategies significantly improve model merging performance across vision and language modalities and multiple model scales.

problem: Long-context adaptation via fine-tuning remains brittle with high positional variance even when controlling for task format and difficulty.
approach: RoPE-Perturbed Self-Distillation forms alternative views by perturbing RoPE indices to move context to different positions and trains via self-distillation for consistent predictions.
contribution: Improves positional robustness with up to 12.04 pp gain on RULER-64K for Llama-3-8B and 2.71 pp on RULER-256K, plus improved length extrapolation.

problem: Static retrieval indices in RAG cause repeated multi-hop traversal for related queries, increasing latency and compute; implementations lack adaptive memory.
approach: GAM-RAG accumulates retrieval experience from recurring queries and updates hierarchical memory over time using Kalman-inspired gain rule for uncertainty-aware updates.
contribution: GAM-RAG improves average performance by 3.95% and by 8.19% with 5-turn memory while reducing inference cost by 61%.

problem: Coresets for clustering provide strong guarantees for all solutions but theoretical sizes are much larger than those sufficient in practice.
approach: Define approximation-preserving coresets providing weaker guarantees for good solutions only (those with low cost), balancing between strong and weak coreset guarantees.
contribution: Smaller approximation-preserving coreset sizes suffice empirically, with complementary lower bounds showing small distortion cannot reduce size further.
